source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 6 iulie — «Sfântul Cuvios Sisoe cel Mare»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 6ης Ιουλίου — «Όσιος Σισώης ο μεγάλος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 6 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and heads him «Οσιος Σισωης ο Μεγαλος (; - 429)»; the folder carries no `dates` object and that year is reported rather than written, because it is the first the corpus has seen for him. The same day's listing carries a second, bare «Όσιος Σισώης», a Russian monk of the eighteenth century with a page of his own; two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, so that is another man and he is drafted separately as `sisoes-the-russian`. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints an apolytikion and more besides, but the extractor cut the page in the middle and no hymn was read whole, so none is taken; that is named in the report.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Locuitor pustiului şi înger în trup şi de minuni făcător te-ai arătat, purtătorule de Dumnezeu, părintele nostru Sisoe; cu postul, cu privegherea, cu rugăciunea, cereşti daruri luând, vindeci pe cei bolnavi şi sufletele celor ce aleargă la tine cu credinţă. Slavă Celui Ce ţi-a dat ţie putere; slavă Celui Ce te-a încununat pe tine; Slavă Celui Ce lucrează prin tine tuturor tămăduiri.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Sisoe cel Mare», Glasul 1

english.text: A dweller of the desert and an angel in the body and a worker of wonders you were shown to be, God-bearing father Sisoes; by fasting, by vigil and by prayer you received heavenly gifts, and you heal the sick and the souls of those who run to you in faith. Glory to Him who gave you strength; glory to Him who crowned you; glory to Him who works healing for all through you.
